newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper editorials - Sept 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper editorials - Sept 16.

text.p: NOTE: These are the highlights of comments carried in the Hong Kong press on Monday. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted, and are not an editorial view of Reuters.

- With 288 days to go before the British colony reverts to China, the Hong Kong media focused mainly on the protests against Japan's claim to the disputed Diaoyu or Senkaku islandsand also addressed Hong Kong's leadership race and the stock exchange.
The middle of the road HONG KONG ECONOMIC JOURNAL said the claim posed a major and unexpected headache for the Chinese government.
Forcing Japan off the islands would be difficult because the Japanese government was afraid of losing its standing among its citizens.
The paper urged Beijing to take immediate measures to solve the dispute and prevent bloodshed or the Taiwanese flag from appearing on the islands.
The Beijing-funded TA KUNG PAO focused on the nomination process for Hong Kong's post-1997 leaders.

It said the month-long nomination process for the Selection Committee had been successful and laid a good foundation for setting up an electoral college that could represent all walks of life in Hong Kong.
It also said the government's decision to bar some senior civil servants from joining the committee violated their rights.
The English-language SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST said moves by some Hong Kong firms to seek listings on the Singapore Stock Exchange posed no cause for alarm.

It said Hong Kong had a massive lead over Singapore in the number of multinational companies establishing headquarters in the territory. If that number started to decline, then it would be time to start worrying.
